**Commentary on Surah "By the Time" (Wa'l-'Asr).** It is Makkan. Qatadah said it is Madinan, and this was also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. It has three verses. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By time (al-'asr),﴾ (1)

There are two issues here.

**The first:** His saying, the Exalted: ﴿By time (wa'l-'asr)﴾ means by the age (ad-dahr). Ibn 'Abbas and others said this. Al-'asr is like ad-dahr, and from it comes the saying of the poet:

"The path of passion is rugged and the sea of passion is deep, / and a day of passion is a month, and a month of passion is an age."

That is, an 'asr (an age). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, swore by it because of the reminder it contains in the changing and alternation of conditions, and the evidence it provides for the Maker. It was also said: al-'asr is the night and the day. Humayd ibn Thawr said:

"The two 'asrs, a day and a night, will not tarry / when they seek to reach what they have set out for."

Al-'asrān also means the morning and the evening. He said:

"I put him off through the two 'asrs until he grows weary of me, / and he accepts half the debt while his nose is rubbed in the dust."

He means: if he comes to me at the beginning of the day, I promise him for the end of it. It was also said that it is the late afternoon (al-'ashiyy), which is the time between the sun's decline from its zenith and its setting. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said this. From it comes the saying of the poet:

"Set out with us in the afternoon, O 'Amr, for the 'asr has grown short, / and in the first setting out lie gain and reward."

It is also reported from Qatadah that it is the last hour of the hours of the day. It was also said that it is an oath by the 'Asr prayer, which is the middle prayer (al-wusta), because it is the most excellent of the prayers. Muqatil said this. One says: "The call was made for the 'asr," meaning for the 'Asr prayer, and "I prayed the 'asr," meaning the 'Asr prayer. In the authentic report: [The middle prayer is the 'Asr prayer]. Its explanation has already been given in Surat al-Baqarah [see vol. 3, p. 210]. It was also said that it is an oath by the era of the Prophet (ﷺ), because of its excellence through the renewal of prophethood in it. It was also said that its meaning is "by the Lord of the 'asr."

**The second:** Malik said: whoever swears not to speak to a man for an 'asr, he may not speak to him for a year. Ibn al-'Arabi said: "Malik interpreted the oath of one who swears not to speak to someone for an 'asr as meaning a year, because that is the longest of what has been said about it, and this follows his principle of taking the stricter sense in oaths. Ash-Shafi'i said: he fulfills his oath with an hour, unless he had an intention. And I say the same, unless the one swearing is an Arab, in which case he is asked: 'What did you intend?' If he explains it with something the word can bear, it is accepted from him, unless it is the shortest possible. According to Malik's school, it should be taken according to what he explains. And Allah knows best."

This is the answer to the oath. What is meant by "the human being" is the disbeliever, as Ibn 'Abbas said in the narration of Abu Salih. Al-Dahhak narrated from him that he said: He means a group of the polytheists: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-'As ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib ibn Asad ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza, and al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth. It is also said that "the human being" means the human race as a whole.

﴿لَفِي خُسْرٍ﴾ means: in loss (ghabn). Al-Akhfash said: in destruction. Al-Farra' said: in punishment, and from this is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿and the outcome of its affair was loss﴾ [al-Talaq: 9]. Ibn Zayd said: in evil. It is also said: in deficiency. The meanings are close to one another.

It is narrated from Sallam that he read (وَالْعَصِرِ) with a kasrah on the sad. Al-A'raj, Talhah and 'Isa al-Thaqafi read (خُسْرٍ) with a dammah on the sin. Harun narrated that from Abu Bakr from 'Asim. The explanation for both readings is ittiba' (assimilation of the vowel to the neighboring one). One says khusr and khusur, like 'usr and 'usur.

'Ali used to recite it: "By the afternoon (al-'asr) and the calamities of time (nawa'ib al-dahr), indeed the human being is in loss, and indeed he is in it until the end of time." Ibrahim said: When a human being lives long in this world and grows old, he is in deficiency, weakness and decline, except for the believers, for there is written for them the rewards of the deeds they used to do in the days of their youth. Similar to this is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿We have certainly created the human being in the best of stature. Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾ [al-Tin: 4-5]. He said: And our recitation is "By the afternoon, indeed the human being is in loss, and indeed he is, at the end of time..."

The correct position is what the Ummah and the mushafs agree upon. The refutation of those who contradict the mushaf of 'Uthman has already been given in the introduction of the book, along with the point that such a reading is not Qur'an to be recited; consider it there.

Commentary on the verse: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Except those who believe﴾ is an exception (istithna') from "the human being" (al-insan), since it carries the meaning of "people" (al-nas), according to the sound view.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ means: they perform the obligatory duties made incumbent upon them. These are the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: I recited to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ﴿By the time (al-'Asr)﴾, then I said: "What is its interpretation, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "﴿By the time﴾ is an oath from Allah; your Lord swore by the end of the day: ﴿Indeed, the human being is in loss﴾: that is Abu Jahl; ﴿except those who believe﴾: Abu Bakr; ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾: 'Umar; ﴿and advise one another to the truth﴾: 'Uthman; ﴿and advise one another to patience﴾: 'Ali," may Allah be pleased with them all. Likewise Ibn 'Abbas preached from the pulpit, this being reported as his own statement (mawquf). The meaning of ﴿and advise one another﴾ (tawasaw) is: they loved one another, each enjoined the other, and each urged the other on.

﴿To the truth﴾ means: to tawhid (the oneness of God). So al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas. Qatadah said: "the truth" means the Qur'an. Al-Suddi said: "the truth" here is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿and advise one another to patience﴾ means: patience in obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and patience in refraining from disobeying Him. This has already been discussed [See p. 71 of this volume]. And Allah knows best.
